sheet.summary: Caln Township's 2023 audit, the only one on file in the 2023 to 2025 window, has one serious finding: a federal COVID recovery funds report was not filed accurately or on time. It is not a repeat and has no questioned costs, so the rating is medium. The finding is not on money passed down by a recognised Virginia state agency, and the audit was filed late (10 months after year end).

reasons.reason: The auditor marked this reporting failure as a material weakness (the most serious kind of control problem) and modified the compliance opinion for the Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds program; no Virginia state agency was recognised as passing this money down.
reasons.quote: The Township did not properly complete and file the report on an accurate, timely basis.

next_checks: Confirm whether audits for 2024 and 2025 exist. None are in the evidence, so 2023 was treated as the latest audit.
Ask for proof that the recovery funds report was corrected and that later reports were filed on time. The Township's plan for the Finance Director to track due dates is a promise, not proof.

Ask why the 2023 audit was accepted 10 months after year end (the limit is nine), and what lies behind the financial-statement material weakness and material noncompliance the audit disclosed, since the evidence has no finding text for them.

sheet.summary: High risk. The latest audit on file (2024) again found that a school construction contract paid with federal COVID relief money (ESSER) left out the required Davis-Bacon wage clause; the auditor called it material noncompliance and it repeats from 2023. Both audits reached the Clearinghouse very late (23 and 32 months after year end), both disclosed a financial-statement material weakness, and no 2025 audit is in the evidence.

reasons.reason: Department of Education money: the latest audit has a serious finding (the auditor modified the compliance opinion on the ESSER school relief program) because a construction contract lacked the required wage clause.
reasons.quote: the contract did not include the required Wage Rate (Davis Bacon Act) and DOL regulations.

reasons.reason: Department of Education money: the auditor says this serious finding is a repeat of last year's, and a serious repeat finding in the latest audit is rated high under the rubric.
reasons.quote: Similar condition present in the prior year.

reasons.reason: Department of Education money: the auditor traces the problem to missing controls, not just a one-time slip, so there is no basis to lower the rating.
reasons.quote: The omission of this clause was due to oversight and a lack of controls in place

reasons.reason: Department of Education money: the earlier audit in the window had the same serious finding on the same program, which is a second route to a high rating.
reasons.quote: did not include the Wage Rate (Davis Bacon Act) and DOL regulations.

reasons.reason: Department of Education and Department of Criminal Justice Services money: the audit package was filed late for the second year running, a repeat finding that touches highway, fiscal recovery and school relief programs.
reasons.quote: The City did not submit the data collection form for the year ended June 30, 2024 timely.

next_checks: Ask the School Board for its current contract template and any federally funded construction contracts signed since June 2024, and confirm the Davis-Bacon wage clause is in them. The locality says procedures are in place; that is a promise, not proof.
Ask the City when the fiscal year 2025 audit will be issued. None is in the evidence, the 2024 audit was accepted 23 months after year end and the 2023 audit 32 months after.

Both audits disclosed a financial-statement material weakness and material noncompliance. Get the 2024 audit report and check whether the 2023 software-conversion problems (wrong fund balances, large audit adjustments) are still open, and confirm which agency passed down the highway and fiscal recovery money, since the pass-through agencies listed for the late-filing finding differ between 2023 and 2024.

sheet.summary: Emporia's latest audit (fiscal year 2024) has five findings, all marked as material weaknesses (the most serious kind of control failure), and one repeats from the prior year, which makes the rating high under the rubric. All five are on Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (21.027) passed through the Department of Criminal Justice Services, and none carries questioned costs. The 2024 audit was accepted 27 months after year end and the 2023 audit 20 months after, and no 2025 audit is on file.

reasons.reason: Department of Criminal Justice Services money: the auditor marked the late audit filing as a material weakness and as a repeat of a prior-year finding, which is what sets the rating at high.
reasons.quote: This was a prior year finding. See Item 2023-001.

reasons.reason: Department of Criminal Justice Services money: the auditor says the City is behind on its required audit filings, so the state is getting audit results long after the money was spent.
reasons.quote: The City has not met its single audit submission requirements.

reasons.reason: Department of Criminal Justice Services money: every payroll timesheet the auditor tested was paid without City approval, a material weakness over what costs are charged to the grant.
reasons.quote: We detected this through sampling in one out of seven disbursements tested and in six out of six payroll timesheets tested.

reasons.reason: Department of Criminal Justice Services money: the City has no written purchasing policy beyond small purchases, which federal rules require, and the auditor marked this as a material weakness.
reasons.quote: The City does not maintain a procurement policy.

reasons.reason: Department of Criminal Justice Services money: a required federal spending report was filed late, and the auditor marked this as a material weakness.
reasons.quote: ARPA Project and Expenditure Report was not filed prior to the deadline date of 4/30/24.

reasons.reason: Department of Criminal Justice Services money: the City's list of federal spending was not checked before the audit and had to be changed, a material weakness in tracking grant money.
reasons.quote: A review of the federal expenditures reported on the SEFA was not performed.

next_checks: Late filing: the 2024 audit was accepted 27 months after year end and the 2023 audit 20 months after (the limit is nine), and no 2025 audit is on file. Ask the City for the status and expected date of the fiscal year 2025 audit.

Verify the City's promised fixes rather than relying on its plan: ask for the adopted written procurement policy (the plan promises it by December 31, 2026), examples of City-approved vendor invoices and timesheets charged to the grant, and the federal reporting schedule.

The 2024 audit cites prior-year finding 2023-001, but no 2023 finding text is in the data provided. Pull the 2023 audit to confirm what it found, and read the 2024 report for the financial-statement material weakness it disclosed.

sheet.summary: Medium risk. The 2025 audit has one finding, marked as a material weakness (the most serious kind of control failure): the City missed or was late with required quarterly reports on its federal COVID recovery funds. It is not a repeat, has no questioned costs, and is on money that came directly from the U.S. Treasury, not through a recognised Virginia state agency; the 2024 and 2025 audits were also filed late.

reasons.reason: The latest audit has a serious finding (a material weakness) on reporting for the Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds, which makes the rating medium; no Virginia state agency was recognised as passing this money down.
reasons.quote: During the fiscal year, the City had Project & Expenditure Reports which were either not submitted or were submitted more than 30 days after the end of the fiscal quarter.

reasons.reason: One required quarterly report was never submitted at all, which shows the failure was more than a short delay; this concerns direct federal money, not a Virginia state agency's.
reasons.quote: The Project & Expenditure Report for the first quarter of the fiscal year was required to be submitted by October 31, 2024, however no report was submitted.

reasons.reason: The auditor ties the cause to weak controls over this one program's reports, not to the whole finance function, so the rating is not moved up to high; again, no Virginia state agency's money is involved.
reasons.quote: The City did not have adequate controls in place to ensure that Project & Expenditure Reports were being filed in a timely manner.

next_checks: Ask the City for proof that the missing first-quarter Project & Expenditure Report was filed and that every later quarterly report went in within 30 days.

Verify the corrective action plan: it says a consulting firm reviewed controls and gives a completion date of December 31, 2026 under an interim finance director. Ask for the firm's report and the new written procedures. The City's response blames staff turnover, so also ask whether reporting on your agency's grants is affected.
Ask why the 2024 and 2025 audits were filed late (accepted 14 and 13 months after year end, against a nine-month limit) and whether the next audit is on schedule.

sheet.summary: Draft rating: high. The 2025 audit has seven federal award findings, five of them material weaknesses (the most serious kind of control failure), and two of those repeat earlier findings. Two are on coronavirus recovery money (21.027) recorded as passed through the Department of Criminal Justice Services; the rest are on workforce and HUD programs with no Virginia state agency recognised. The 2025 and 2024 audits were also filed late, at 15 and 13 months after year end.

reasons.reason: No Virginia state agency recognised (workforce programs): this 2025 finding is a material weakness and the auditor marks it as a repeat of the prior year, which makes the rating high under the rubric.
reasons.quote: Repeat Finding 2024-002

reasons.reason: No Virginia state agency recognised (workforce programs): the same failure to monitor subrecipients was already reported in 2024, when it was itself a repeat of 2023, so it has now run three years.
reasons.quote: There was a lack of evidence of testing and suggestions to the subrecipient during the fiscal year 2024.

reasons.reason: No Virginia state agency recognised (HUD lead hazard grant): a second 2025 material weakness that repeats finding 2024-003, because nobody reviews reports before they are sent.
reasons.quote: we noted that the City lacked a review process

reasons.reason: Department of Criminal Justice Services (coronavirus recovery funds): a new 2025 material weakness, because the City did not monitor the organisations it passed this money to.
reasons.quote: Subrecipient monitoring was not done according the City’s formal, written policy

reasons.reason: Department of Criminal Justice Services (coronavirus recovery funds): a new 2025 material weakness, because the spending reported to the federal government did not match the City's own records and the backup could not be produced.
reasons.quote: cumulative totals of expenditures did not agree to the total amounts reported on the

reasons.reason: No Virginia state agency recognised (HUD lead hazard grant): required financial reports were not filed at all, which led the auditor to modify the opinion on compliance for this program.
reasons.quote: quarterly reports were not submitted.

reasons.reason: No rating change, since high is already the top level, but the auditor traces findings in several programs to the same finance staffing gap, which points to a systemic problem (Department of Criminal Justice Services money included).
reasons.quote: Staff turnover, including the lack of a grant accountant.

next_checks: Confirm which of the 23 coronavirus recovery fund (21.027) awards in findings 2025-006 and 2025-007 are actually Department of Criminal Justice Services money, and whether the subrecipient monitoring and reporting failures touch those awards.

Ask the City for proof of its claimed fixes rather than relying on its plan: evidence that a grant accountant is in post, completed subrecipient desk-monitoring files, and the reconciliation it says was done for the quarter ending June 30, 2026.

Ask why the 2025 audit was accepted 15 months after year end and the 2024 audit 13 months after (the limit is nine), and get details of the material weakness and material noncompliance the 2025 audit disclosed at the financial-statement level, which have no finding text here.

sheet.summary: Staunton's latest audit (2025) has three findings on federal awards, which makes the rating medium under the rubric. None is a material weakness (the most serious kind of control failure), none is a repeat and none has questioned costs. All three are about missing paperwork or undocumented reviews; no adjustment up or down was made from the text.

reasons.reason: Department of Social Services money: this is one of three findings in the latest audit, which sets the rating at medium, though the auditor found the missing supervisor sign-off in only one Adoption Assistance file.
reasons.quote: In one instance, there was no evidence of supervisory approval on any forms.

reasons.reason: Department of Education and Department of Health money: the second 2025 finding shows the city passed Coronavirus recovery funds to another body without giving it the required federal award details.
reasons.quote: All necessary information was not communicated to the subrecipient.

reasons.reason: No Virginia state agency's money (Community Development Block Grant): the third 2025 finding shows grant reports went out without a documented review, which brings the count to three.
reasons.quote: There was no evidence of review of two of the five reports tested.

reasons.reason: No Virginia state agency's money (Coronavirus recovery funds): an earlier audit also found a review weakness, but it was not a serious finding and does not raise the rating.
reasons.quote: review of the revenue loss calculation did not detect this error.

next_checks: Department of Social Services: ask for a sample of fiscal year 2026 Adoption Assistance eligibility files and confirm each shows both the case worker's and the supervisor's signature or initials, as the city promised.

Department of Education and Department of Health: ask for the city's current subaward documents for Coronavirus recovery funds and confirm they now state the federal award number (FAIN), the program number (ALN) and the federal awarding agency.

Confirm the city can show documented review of grant reports before submission from the quarter ended 9/30/2025 onward; the city says it has done this, but that is its own statement, not the auditor's.

sheet.summary: Low risk. The only finding in the 2023 to 2025 window is from the 2023 audit: the County filed its 2022 audit reporting form late. The 2024 and 2025 audits have no findings on federal awards, and no audit in the window disclosed a material weakness, material noncompliance or going-concern doubt.

reasons.reason: The only finding in the window is in an earlier audit (2023), not the latest (2025), which the rubric rates low; it is a late filing, not misspent money, and it touches programs passed down by the Departments of Agriculture and Consumer Services, Criminal Justice Services, Education and Social Services.
reasons.quote: The County did not file the data collection form for the year ended June 30, 2022 timely.

reasons.reason: The auditor put the cause on management missing a deadline and marked the finding as a repeat, but not as a material weakness or significant deficiency and with no questioned costs, so no adjustment to the low rating is made; this applies to all four pass-through agencies named above.
reasons.quote: Management did not complete and certify auditee portion of the form before the deadline.

next_checks: Confirm the County is still filing on time: the 2025 audit was accepted on 2026-03-25, about nine months after year end and only days inside the deadline.

Ask the County for evidence that the staffing fixes promised in its 2023 corrective action plan (vacancies filled, one position added, finance department restructured) are in place and holding. The plan is a promise, not proof.
The 2023 finding was marked as a repeat. Look at the 2022 audit, which is outside this window, to see how long late filing had been a problem.

sheet.summary: Medium. The latest audit on file (2024) has one finding, and it repeats the 2023 finding: the County has no complete written procurement policy that meets federal rules. The auditor did not mark it as a material weakness (the most severe kind of control problem) and questioned no costs, but it went unfixed for a year.

reasons.reason: Department of Education money: the latest audit found the County still lacks written purchasing rules that meet federal standards, and the auditor flagged this as a repeat finding, which makes the rating medium.
reasons.quote: The County does not have its own written procurement policies that conform to applicable Federal laws and regulations and standards.

reasons.reason: Department of Education money: the auditor says the gap could lead to improper purchases with federal funds, though no costs were questioned.
reasons.quote: could result in potential improper procurement using Federal funds.

reasons.reason: No Virginia state agency was recognised for this finding: the same problem was first reported the year before, which shows it stayed open for a full audit cycle.
reasons.quote: The County does not have its own written procurement policies that conform to applicable Federal laws

next_checks: Ask the County for its adopted written procurement policy and confirm it covers the federal standards in 2 CFR 200.317 to 200.326. Its corrective action plans in both 2023 and 2024 said only that updating had begun.
No 2025 audit is in the evidence, although the review window runs to 2025. Check whether it has been filed, whether it was filed on time, and whether the procurement finding repeats a third time.

Confirm which Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds awards the 2024 finding covers. It lists two awards and names the Department of Education, while the 2023 finding names no state agency.

sheet.summary: Floyd County's 2025 audit has three findings on federal awards, two of them serious, all touching Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds passed through the Department of Criminal Justice Services and the Department of Housing and Community Development. None is a repeat or flagged with questioned costs, and 2023 and 2024 show no federal award findings, so the rating is medium. I did not move it up, but the reviewer should weigh two things: the missing procurement manual spans several programs, and the 2025 and 2024 audits were filed late (14 and 13 months after year end).

reasons.reason: For the Department of Criminal Justice Services and the Department of Housing and Community Development: the auditor gave a modified opinion on compliance for the recovery funds because reported spending could not be backed up, which makes this a serious finding.
reasons.quote: No supporting documentation for key line items on P&E expenditure report.

reasons.reason: For the Department of Criminal Justice Services and the Department of Housing and Community Development: the auditor marked as a material weakness (the most severe kind of control failure) that the County left grant spending off its schedule of federal spending (the SEFA).
reasons.quote: The SEFA was understated by $175,000 for the E&T LE Grant.

reasons.reason: For the Department of Education, the Department of Criminal Justice Services and the Department of Housing and Community Development: this is the third finding in the latest audit, and it covers both the school nutrition programs and the recovery funds.
reasons.quote: The County does not have a Uniform Guidance Procurement Manual.

next_checks: Confirm whether finding 2025-017 carries questioned costs. The data flag says no, but the auditor's text has a line reading "Questioned Cost Amount P&E report was understated by $186,000." If it does count, a serious finding with questioned costs makes the rating high.

Ask for proof that the County's promised fixes are done: an adopted procurement manual covering all departments, a corrected and documented P&E report, and a SEFA built from an expenditure listing and reconciled to the Cardinal Report. The County's plan is a promise, not evidence.

Ask why the 2025 and 2024 audits were filed late (14 and 13 months after year end), and what the financial-statement material weakness disclosed in each of 2023, 2024 and 2025 was. The data here has no finding text for those.

sheet.summary: Low risk under the rubric. The latest audit (2025) has one finding, on Department of Social Services money: late Medicaid eligibility reviews, not marked as a material weakness (the most serious kind of control failure), not repeated and with no questioned costs. A 2023 finding on workforce grants led to a modified opinion (the auditor could not give that program a clean compliance opinion), and the 2025 audit also flags material noncompliance without finding text, so both need a look.

reasons.reason: Department of Social Services (Medicaid): the only finding in the latest audit is late eligibility reviews, with no serious, repeat or questioned-cost flags, which puts the rating at low.
reasons.quote: In 4 of the 25 cases tested, eligibility redetermination had not been completed

reasons.reason: No Virginia state agency recognised in the data (the auditor names the Virginia Community College System as the pass-through for workforce grants): this earlier finding led to a modified compliance opinion, but it is not in the latest audit, so it does not raise the rating.
reasons.quote: The Workforce Development Board has not had a current audit in accordance with Uniform Guidance.

next_checks: Department of Social Services: ask for evidence that the overdue Medicaid eligibility reviews are caught up and that supervisors are doing the monthly report reviews promised in the county's plan. The plan also depends on filling a vacant manager position, so confirm whether it is filled. The plan is a promise, not proof.
The 2025 audit is flagged as disclosing material noncompliance, but the data has no finding text that explains it. Get the full 2025 audit report and find out what it refers to.

Workforce grants (2023 finding): confirm the West Piedmont Workforce Development Board has since had a current audit and that the county is monitoring it. The finding did not recur in 2024 or 2025, but the data does not say it was fixed.

sheet.summary: Low under the rubric: the only federal award finding in the 2023 to 2025 window is one from 2023, and the latest audit (2025) has none. This is not a clean bill of health. All three audits disclosed a material weakness (a serious control gap) in the financial statements with no finding text here, and all three were filed late.

reasons.reason: The only federal award finding in the window is from an earlier audit: a repeat reporting finding, not marked serious and with no questioned costs, on Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds, with no Virginia state agency recognised as passing the money down.
reasons.quote: Per program requirements, a Project and Expenditure Report (P&E) was due by April 30, 2023 and annually thereafter.

next_checks: Get the financial-statement findings from the 2023, 2024 and 2025 audit reports. Each audit disclosed a material weakness, but no finding text is in this data, so we cannot tell what it was or whether it touches grant accounting.

Confirm the Project and Expenditure Reports due April 30, 2024 and later were filed on time. The county says the 2024 report was, but that is its own statement, not the auditor's. The 2023 finding text also does not say what went wrong, so read the full finding.
Ask why all three audits were filed late (accepted 12, 11 and 10 months after year end, against a nine-month limit) and whether the 2026 audit is on schedule.

sheet.summary: Low under the rubric: the only federal award finding in the window is from 2024, and the latest audit (2025) has none. That 2024 finding was over-claimed school meal reimbursements with questioned costs, on money passed through the Department of Education and the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services. This is not a clean bill of health: the 2024 and 2025 audits both disclosed a material weakness and material noncompliance with no finding text in the data, and the 2023 and 2024 audits were filed late.

reasons.reason: The only finding in the window is in an earlier audit (2024), and it carries questioned costs on school nutrition money passed through the Department of Education and the Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services; the 2025 audit has no federal award findings, so the rubric gives low.
reasons.quote: There are likely questioned costs of $124,430 (consisting of $24,886 in known questioned costs) related to over claiming school nutrition reimbursements.

reasons.reason: The auditor found a small number of errors in a sample of meal claims (Department of Education and Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services money), which does not show a problem across the finance function, so the rating is not moved up.
reasons.quote: We reviewed 26 school submissions out of the 130 annual submissions and noted 2 errors.

reasons.reason: The auditor traces the cause to manual entry mistakes, not missing staff or absent controls, but the text does not say the errors were corrected before the audit was issued, so the rating is not moved down either.
reasons.quote: Reimbursements require manual data entry and amounts were requested in error.

next_checks: Get the full 2025 and 2024 audit reports and read what the disclosed material weakness and material noncompliance were. The data flags both in each year but gives no finding text, and the County was not a low-risk auditee in 2025.

Confirm with the School Board and the Department of Education that the meal-count review process is actually in place, and whether the over-claimed February 2024 reimbursement ($24,886 known, $124,430 likely) was repaid or resolved. The plan on file only repeats the auditor's recommendation and is not proof of a fix.
Ask why the 2024 audit was accepted 10 months and the 2023 audit 15 months after year end, both past the nine-month deadline. The 2025 audit was on time at 8 months.

sheet.summary: Draft rating: low. The latest audit (2025) has one finding on the school meal programs. It is a significant deficiency (a control gap less severe than a material weakness), not a repeat, with no questioned costs. The only earlier finding (2023) is also a significant deficiency. No adjustment from the text was made: both findings are missing paperwork in the school system, which is worth watching but is not shown to be systemic.

reasons.reason: Department of Education and Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (school breakfast and lunch): the latest audit found no proof that a second person checked three monthly reimbursement requests, which is a control gap but not a serious finding under the rubric.
reasons.quote: was no evidence of adequate segregation of duties between the preparation of the reimbursement

reasons.reason: Department of Education and Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services: the auditor found no questioned costs on this finding, so nothing pushes the rating above low.
reasons.quote: There are no questioned costs related to this finding

reasons.reason: Department of Social Services per the data, though the finding text names the Department of Education (COVID recovery funds): the earlier audit found a missing record of a vendor exclusion check, which was a lesser finding and does not raise the rating.
reasons.quote: The suspension and debarment status for one out of two vendors was not retained

reasons.reason: Same agency question as above: the auditor confirmed the vendors were not excluded and no costs were questioned, so the 2023 problem was missing paperwork rather than a wrongful payment.
reasons.quote: There are no questioned costs related to this finding as the vendors were not federally suspended or debarred.

next_checks: Ask the school system for recent monthly meal reimbursement requests showing sign-off by someone other than the preparer. The corrective action plan says this now happens, but that is a promise, not proof.

The 2023 audit is on file twice: once accepted 9 months after year end and again 17 months after. Find out why it was resubmitted and whether anything changed. Finding 2023-001 appears twice in the data, probably for this reason.

Confirm which agency owns finding 2023-001: the data lists the Department of Social Services, but the finding text names the Virginia Department of Education. Also ask for proof that vendor exclusion checks are now kept on file.

sheet.summary: Low under the rubric, because the only federal-award finding in the window is from 2023 and the 2024 and 2025 audits have none. That 2023 finding was serious: a repeat finding with questioned costs on Department of Education money, and the data supplied holds almost none of the auditor's text for it. Reported beside the rating: all three audits disclosed a financial-statement material weakness (a serious gap in financial controls), and the 2025 audit was filed late, 10 months after year end.

reasons.reason: This concerns the Department of Education: the only finding in the window is this 2023 one on Education Stabilization Fund money, flagged as a material weakness, a modified compliance opinion, a repeat finding and questioned costs, but it sits in an earlier audit and the latest audit (2025) has no findings, which the rubric rates low.
reasons.quote: Program Titles: Education Stabilization Fund

next_checks: Pull the full 2023 audit report for finding 2023-003 (Department of Education, Education Stabilization Fund). The data here has no auditor narrative, so confirm what went wrong, the amount of questioned costs, and whether they were resolved or repaid.

Verify that the county did what its plan promised: reviewing how it requests reimbursements and reconciles them to the ledger. The plan is a promise, not proof; ask for evidence and confirm the 2024 and 2025 audits tested this program area.

Ask why the 2025 audit was accepted 10 months after year end (late), and read the financial-statement material weakness disclosed in each of 2023, 2024 and 2025, since the data carries no finding text for it.

sheet.summary: High risk. The latest audit (2024) found that late payment of contractors and vendors on federal transit grants was a material weakness (the most serious kind of control failure) and a repeat of the 2023 finding. None of the findings is on money passed down by a recognised Virginia state agency, and both audits were filed on time (7 and 9 months after year end). No 2025 audit is in the evidence.

reasons.reason: The latest audit has a serious finding (a material weakness that also led to a modified compliance opinion) flagged as a repeat, which makes the rating high under step 2; it is on Federal Transit Formula Grants (20.507), with no Virginia state agency recognised as the pass-through.
reasons.quote: We noted 14 instances where contractors and vendors were not paid for over 30 days. We also noted four vendors were not paid for over 90 days.

reasons.reason: The earlier audit in the window also had a serious finding on the same late-payment problem, which is a second, separate ground for high; it is on federal transit grants (20.500 and 20.507), with no Virginia state agency recognised.
reasons.quote: Contractors were not paid for over 30 days after receipt of invoice.

reasons.reason: A lesser finding (a significant deficiency) shows expired grants were left open with money still on them, which adds to the picture of weak grant management; it is on 20.507, with no Virginia state agency recognised.
reasons.quote: All 6 were still marked as active in the grant award management system as of June 30, 2024, with total remaining funds on these awards totaling $673,179.

reasons.reason: A third finding in the latest audit shows required federal contract clauses were missing, a minor compliance gap that does not change the rating; it is on 20.507, with no Virginia state agency recognised.
reasons.quote: did not contain these clauses in one contract tested

next_checks: Ask for proof that vendors are now paid on time and grant draws are made promptly: the locality's plan promises a monthly close checklist, grant tracking spreadsheets and filling vacant finance posts, but the same finding repeated from 2023 to 2024 despite a similar promise.

Confirm whether the six expired federal grants (with $673,179 remaining) have been closed out, and whether the missing contract clauses have been added to the procurement manual and contract templates.

Check whether the 2025 audit has been filed, since none is in the evidence. Also note both the 2023 and 2024 audits disclosed a material weakness and material noncompliance at the financial-statement level, and confirm whether any of your agency's money goes to this locality, as no Virginia pass-through agency was recognised on these findings.

sheet.summary: Low under the rubric, because the only federal-award finding in the window is from 2023 and the latest audit (2025) has none. That 2023 finding was serious: it was a repeat, carried questioned costs, and led the auditor to modify the compliance opinion on three workforce (WIOA) programs. Treat the low rating with caution: all three audits were filed late, and each disclosed a material weakness and material noncompliance that the data gives no finding text for.

reasons.reason: The only finding in the window is in the 2023 audit, not the latest one, so the rubric gives low; it concerns WIOA money that the auditor says came through the Virginia Community College System (the data matched no Virginia state agency), and the County let its subrecipient draw funds unreviewed.
reasons.quote: Funds are requested for drawdown by the subrecipient without the County reviewing

reasons.reason: I did not move the rating up: the finding covers three programs, but the auditor ties it to one misunderstood requirement for one subrecipient on Virginia Community College System money, not to a breakdown across the finance function.
reasons.quote: The County misunderstood the compliance requirements for subrecipient monitoring.

next_checks: Get the 2024 and 2025 audit reports. Both disclosed a material weakness and material noncompliance, but the data has no findings for those years. Confirm what those were and whether finding 2023-007 came back or was closed.
Ask why all three audits were late: accepted 16, 17 and 15 months after year end, against a nine-month limit.

Verify the County's plan was carried out: that it now reviews the workforce board's financial records and gets its annual audit, and that it reviews and approves drawdown requests, which the plan does not mention. Also find the amount of the 2023 questioned costs, which the finding text does not state, and whether they were resolved.

sheet.summary: Draft rating: high. The 2024 audit, the only one in the 2023 to 2025 window, has three findings the auditor marked as material weaknesses (the most serious kind of control failure), which is medium by the rubric's flags. I moved it up one level because the auditor traces all three to finance staff turnover and missing backup controls, across two programs passed through the Department of Health and the Department of Transportation. The audit was also filed 17 months after year end and disclosed material noncompliance.

reasons.reason: Concerns Department of Health and Department of Transportation money: bank accounts were not reconciled on time, and the auditor marked this as a material weakness, which makes the base rating medium.
reasons.quote: The Commission is not timely reconciling the bank accounts.

reasons.reason: Concerns Department of Health and Department of Transportation money: the Commission's list of federal spending by award was not reliable, a second material weakness in the latest audit.
reasons.quote: The Commission did not have sufficient controls to ensure the SEFA accurately reflected each award

reasons.reason: Concerns Department of Health and Department of Transportation money: the audit was filed late, a third material weakness, so the latest audit has three findings in all.
